slides.prompt: What do you do every day?
slides.notes: 60-min Mon lesson, 31 Aug, 2:20-3:20. Retrieval bridges Week 30 hobby phrases into daily routines. Outcome (teacher-kept): describe a morning routine in four connected simple-present sentences.
Retrieval of Week 30 verb phrases from 24/27 Aug decks. Reveal one step at a time; class choruses each phrase. Non-digital fallback: chorus.
Retrieval of Week 30 place/time chunks. Same scaffold reused for routines today so the language load is use, not new vocabulary.

slides.prompt: What is different about a routine?

columns.label: Hobby
columns.text: What you love to do, sometimes.

slides.notes: Bridge: hobby (sometimes) vs routine (every day). Expected: routine means every day, so we use simple present. Grammar book: present simple for regular-basis actions.

slides.prompt: What changes with he and she?
slides.notes: Model: He/She adds -s (wakes, plays). Routine is present simple, never is + -ing. Listen for I am wake up.
Click fills the blank inline; Reset clears it. B is for I/you. C needs is. Listen for She brush.

slides.prompt: Where do the time and place go?
slides.answer: At the end: at home at 7 o'clock.
slides.hint: Look at the end of the sentence.
slides.notes: Model: I have breakfast at home at 7 o'clock. Grammar book: phrasal time/place adverbials at end, place before time. Never in the middle of the verb.

slides.prompt: Make three true sentences about your morning.
slides.hint: Use a verb with where and when.
slides.notes: Elicit 3 oral sentences from verb x where x when grid: wake up / have breakfast / go to school; at home / by bus; at 6.30 a.m. / 7 o'clock / 7.30 a.m. Formula: who + verb + where + when.

slides.sentence: I wake up early {{blank}} I like morning assembly.
slides.feedback: Because gives a reason. And only adds.
slides.hint: Do you add or explain why?
slides.notes: Click fills the blank inline; Reset clears it. Grammar book: because marks reason; and marks addition. Listen for and-chaining.

slides.prompt: Say the four guide words in order.
slides.notes: Reuse of Week 30 linkers with fronted comma for time order. Reveal one step at a time; class choruses.

slides.prompt: Put the morning in time order.
items: Firstly, I wake up at 6.30 a.m.
Besides that, I brush my teeth at 6.45 a.m.
Then, I have breakfast at home.
Finally, I go to school at 7.30 a.m.
slides.notes: Items shown reversed; pupils click in sequence, click again to remove. Reveal restores time order. Ask why Finally cannot be first.

slides.task: Write four sentences about Amira's morning from 6.30 to 7.30. Use She and the four guide words.
slides.frame: Firstly, Amira ... Besides that, she ... Then, she ... Finally, she ...
slides.notes: Shared scaffold: Amira wakes up 6.30, brushes teeth at home 6.45, breakfast because she needs energy, school 7.30. Frame revealed on request. Watch She + -s throughout.

slides.feedback: Time goes at the end. She needs has.
slides.hint: Check the time and the verb.
slides.notes: Repair check: A puts time in the middle; B misses -s. Selection records attempt; Reveal explains.

slides.prompt: Tell your partner about your morning in four sentences.
slides.hint: Use Firstly, Besides that, Then, Finally.
slides.notes: 2-min partner talk. A talks, B listens for -s and time at the end, then switch. Formula: present simple + time at the end + because if you can.

slides.prompt: Write four sentences about your morning.
slides.hint: Use three guide words and because or and once.
slides.notes: 5-min individual exit, no model. Expect 3 linkers and 1 because/and; look for present simple, -s for he/she, time/place at end. Copying the class model without personalising is not mastery.

slides.prompt: What do we use for routines?
slides.answer: Present simple: She wakes up every day.
slides.feedback: Who plus verb plus where plus when.
slides.notes: Close: routine means every day, so present simple; because gives a reason. Forward bridge: add evening routine into one whole-day paragraph.
